done_when: src/forge/standards.md, src/forge/templates/conventions/testing.md, src/forge/templates/brief.md and src/forge/templates/review.md all say: every Done-when item is proven by an end-to-end test through the real entry point (Forge's own command; for client apps, the running API with a real database and user flows in a browser through Playwright), faking only third-party services at their edge; unit tests only for pure logic with many cases and never as an item's only proof; review reports an item proven only by unit tests as a P1 Not done and never asks for unit tests of helpers; a test pins each of the four texts

findings.body: The first three tests only call this shared assertion, which omits the requirements to report unit-only proof as P1 `Not done` and never request helper unit tests. Removing that entire sentence from standards.md, templates/conventions/testing.md, or templates/brief.md leaves all four new tests passing; only review.md has assertions protecting it. The Done-when requires these rules in all four texts and tests pinning them. Add the missing assertions for the other three texts.
findings.title: Not done: pin the P1 and helper-unit-test rules in all four guidance texts

why: Forge's test guidance doesn't put end-to-end tests first: workers add narrow unit tests and review sometimes asks for unit tests of helpers, while nothing requires each Done-when item to be proven through the real entry point
